_comment: Towns allowed to be delivered with a STALE S6 verification, and until when.
scripts/deliver-map.mjs refuses a town whose latest S6 run pre-dates its
newest S1/S2/S3 data (technical-audit_2026-08-19 V3): the byte gates prove
the renderer reproduces the sheet, S6 is the stage that asks whether the
sheet is RIGHT, and on 2026-08-19 every town was stale by 8-31 days while
all 13 maps were live.
This file exists because that gate would otherwise have been RED on its
first run, for all eight towns, and a check that is red on day one gets
muted inside a week - the audit's own V4 names gate fatigue as a live
problem here. Same shape and same reasoning as scripts/audit-allowlist.json:
an entry is a DEFERRAL, not a waiver, and deliver-map.mjs refuses an entry
whose `until` has passed just as loudly as it refuses a missing one. A
deferral has to be renewed deliberately; it cannot rot into a permanent
exemption nobody re-reads.
TO CLEAR ONE: run the town's S6 stage (make-bus-leaflet, stage S6) against
its current data, then delete its entry here. Do not extend `until` without
writing down what changed.
ST NEOTS WAS REMOVED ON 2026-08-20, the day this file was written, because
its S6 was actually run. A separate session refreshed the town against a
same-day BODS feed (S3 09:23, then S6 09:26) and the gate now reports it as
verified rather than deferred. That is the whole intended lifecycle of an
entry here, and it happened on the first real encounter: run S6, delete the
row. Seven towns remain.
The `until` dates are staggered so eight towns' S6 passes do not all fall
due in the same week.
2026-08-26 - ALL SEVEN S6 RUNS WERE DONE (audit N16). Two passed and their
rows are deleted: St Ives (0 hard / 11 soft) and Beaconsfield (0 hard / 22
soft). Five came back BLOCKED and their rows are left exactly as they were,
at the client's instruction to report rather than change: Huntingdon (1
hard), High Wycombe (1 hard), Wisbech (2 hard), March (1 hard), Ramsey (14
hard). Every run is committed in its town's manifest with a verification.docx.

FIXED 2026-08-28 (OA-003, OA-133) - the paragraph that used to sit here said the gate could not tell a passing S6 from a failing one, and it can now. scripts/lib/s6-freshness.mjs opens the latest run's verification.json and reads summary.verdict (pass | blocked | not-verified-uncurated-s1, with summary.pass as the fallback for runs stored before that field existed). Its verdicts are now fresh | stale | never | failed | unverified | no-verdict | not-applicable | no-manifest, and deliver-map.mjs consults THIS FILE for every one of them that refuses - not just STALE, which was the second half of the same bug: the five BLOCKED towns below were being accepted while carrying live deferrals that had silently stopped applying to them.

AND PLACES ARE NO LONGER EXEMPT. The gate used to return not-applicable for every place, on the premise that the place skill has no verification stage. It gained one on 2026-08-08 (place_verified_services.js), the procedure is written up in make-bus-leaflet/references/s6-verify.md, and two places hold real runs. A place is now judged exactly as an area is.

WHICH IS WHY TEN PLACE ROWS APPEAR BELOW, all reading `never`. That is true of every one of them and it is the day-one red this file exists for. It is not a cheap debt: measured 2026-08-28, redteam_source.js answers BUY for all ten, because it only ever looks inside a build's OWN S6-verify/ and a place has never had one - so none of them can reuse its parent town's answer. At the measured 89k-137k tokens per red team that is roughly a million tokens, two or three sessions' work. Whether a place may legitimately reuse its town's answer is an open question, not a settled no; see the open action.

TWO PLACES ARE ALREADY CLEAR and have no row here: St Neots Town Centre and St Neots Tesco Extra, both PASS on 2026-08-28 after OA-049 taught S6 to read the `notShown` declaration. They are the proof that these rows can be retired the intended way.
passed, and the gate cannot tell the difference. scripts/lib/s6-freshness.mjs
compares DATES ONLY - its verdicts are fresh/stale/never/not-applicable/
no-manifest - and it never opens verification.json or reads summary.pass. So
as of these runs all five BLOCKED towns report `fresh` to deliver-map.mjs and
would be accepted as verified. Their rows below no longer protect them
either: gateS6() consults this file only when the verdict is STALE, so a
fresh-but-failing S6 skips the waiver check entirely. Before today those five
were at least STALE and deferred with an expiry; now they are silently green.
The fix is for the freshness check to read the verdict as well as the date,
and to fail on hard>0 - which will start red for five towns, so it needs
dated exceptions in the same spirit as this file rather than being switched
on bare.
Two `why` lines below are known to misattribute, corrected here rather than
edited in place. RAMSEY's says 'S6 predates the P1-round config pass', the
same wording as St Ives, which passes. That is not Ramsey's problem: Ramsey
is an unattended Tier-2 auto-draft (its own routes.json says so, and see
Areas/Ramsey/DRAFT-REVIEW.md), its S1 was never curated, and its 2026-08-08
S6 already reported 9 hard - byte-identical to today's sanity findings. It
was published under a staleness deferral while its own verification said
BLOCKED. WISBECH's mentions the X46 palette repick; today's red team says
X46 may no longer exist as a separate service at all, having been merged
into the plain 46, and we still draw it.
Also note the `dataAsAt` values below are all stale: they say 2026-08-19,
but every town's newest S3 is 2026-08-24_1600 (the opt-in rebase). The rows
understate their own staleness by five days.
